title: 1993 census
text: Power Unlimited 1993 contains 209 separately scored evaluations across PU #001–#005. Mean 7.7928, median 8.0, 9+ count 41. Scores remain on the 10-point scale.

title: Reviewer ranking
text: Among reviewers with at least 20 solo evaluations, statistically strictest is Michael Schaeffer at 7.388; mildest is David Lemereis at 8.4. Michael Schaefer/Schaeffer grouping is a high-confidence year-level identity inference, not a rewritten source spelling.

title: Platform ranking policy
text: Platform stats normalize only obvious printed aliases. Composite labels such as PC / Macintosh are kept separate and are not duplicated into both means. Platform versions that received separate scores remain separate evaluations.

title: 3DO
text: Across the five issues, 3DO moves from extraordinary future-facing claims, through explicit skepticism about demonstrations and hype, to a real Netherlands hands-on encounter that causes PU to revise its earlier caution. This is a synthesis inference, not a single contemporaneous PU verdict.

title: Atari Jaguar
text: Jaguar begins as a 64-bit rumor/report, is described in issue 2 with an onboard double-speed compact disc, is challenged by a reader in issue 3 and reframed as cartridge hardware with optional CD expansion, then becomes a confirmed hands-on machine in issue 5.

title: Virtual Reality
text: The corpus does not contain one unified PU position on VR. Issue 2 contains both near-term Sega VR expectation and a positive long-term prediction after a primitive demo; issue 3 prints Laurens Stolker rejecting VR; issue 4 prints Edward Laauwen predicting VR games as the future. These voices must remain distinct.

title: Amiga CD32
text: CD32 becomes visible partly through reader pressure: an Amiga reader criticizes PU for overlooking the platform, PU says it will wait and speak to Commodore, and the same issue contains substantive CD32 coverage describing it as a 32-bit CD console already in shops.

title: 3DO
text: Issue 5 explicitly recalls earlier caution about 3DO and then reports a working machine with software, making this an internally documented revision of confidence.

title: Atari Jaguar CD configuration
text: Issue 2 says Jaguar contains a double-speed compact disc; issue 3 reader feedback disputes this, and later coverage treats CD as an expansion/add-on rather than the core cartridge medium.

title: Virtual Reality future
text: Positive and negative future claims coexist across different speakers and articles. YEAR_SYNTHESIS must not collapse them into a single PU prediction.

title: Project Reality
text: Issue 5 carries a prediction that Project Reality would bring Jurassic Park-like technology into the home within about two years. This package records the prediction only and does not test it against external reality.

title: Mortal Kombat / Ermac
text: Issue 5 reports Ermac as a mysterious player anecdote and explicitly asks readers to help investigate. The synthesis preserves it as a contemporary mystery report, not established game fact.

title: PREVIEW terminology
text: A reader in issue 2 challenges the use of PREVIEW for import games. PU then repeatedly publishes a house definition in which REVIEW/BESPREKING tracks broad Dutch availability and PREVIEW/VOORBESPREKING tracks specialist/import/rental availability.

title: Super Mario Kart
text: Bjorn scores Super Mario Kart 6.5 in issue 1. Issue 2 publishes reader disagreement. Issue 4 explicitly says the earlier judgement produced many angry reactions and revisits the game in Eeuwig Leven. No replacement score is printed, so this is a re-evaluation framing rather than a score correction.

title: The Lost Vikings
text: The Lost Vikings becomes a months-long reader/editor knowledge loop: the issue 2 review is followed by issue 3 reader-supplied endgame codes after Bjorn became stuck, issue 4 reader complaints about promised codes, and issue 5 another reader solution for level 38.

title: Asterix
text: Issue 3 records a reader request asking PU to put Asterix on Super NES in that very issue; the issue contains scored Asterix evaluations. This shows the letters layer and review layer intersecting, although timing does not prove the letter caused the review.

title: Core redaction expansion
text: Issue 1 masthead lists Bjorn Bruinsma, Ben de Dood, Adam Eeuwens, Kees de Koning and David Lemereis under Redaktie, while Michael Schaeffer is a contributor. Issue 2 adds Michael to Redaktie, and issues 3-5 keep a six-person core.

title: Michael surname spelling
text: The corpus spells the editor/contributor surname Schaeffer in issue 1 and issues 3-5, but Schaefer in issue 2. YEAR_SYNTHESIS groups these only for inferred year-level statistics and preserves every source spelling.
